subject.title: fix(memory-lancedb): gate auto-recall/auto-capture on per-agent memorySearch.enabled (#103590)

question: Should this PR land a corrected memorySearch.enabled gate as immediate containment, or must memory-lancedb also partition persisted records by agent before the disclosure is considered fixed?
rationale: The linked issue and earlier unmerged isolation proposals show materially different security, compatibility, and legacy-data outcomes that cannot be selected safely from implementation details alone.

options.title: Land containment first
options.body: Correct the normalized gate, prove disabled agents neither recall nor capture automatically, and track persisted-record isolation and legacy-row treatment separately.

options.title: Require full isolation now
options.body: Expand the fix to agent-scoped persistence with an explicit migration or disposition for existing shared records before merge.

options.title: Preserve shared storage
options.body: Treat shared records as intentional and document that memorySearch.enabled controls automatic participation rather than complete agent isolation.

recommendation.title: Land containment first
recommendation.body: Correct the normalized gate, prove disabled agents neither recall nor capture automatically, and track persisted-record isolation and legacy-row treatment separately.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest available history signal across core memory search, the LanceDB implementation, and compatibility-sensitive configuration behavior.
